analysis.subject: maths
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers how to calculate one-month, twelve-month and annual average percent changes from CPI index values using subtraction, division and multiplication by 100 with worked examples in tables

overview.headline: Calculating monthly, yearly and annual average percent change from index values

keyPoints.point: Students learn that percent change is found when you subtract the earlier index value from the later value, divide that difference by the earlier index value and multiply by 100
keyPoints.quote: you first subtract the earlier index value from the later one, then divide that difference by the earlier index value

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a twelve-month percent change must use the same month for beginning and ending periods, such as December to December
keyPoints.quote: the beginning and ending periods of a CPI series must always be the same month, such as December 2021 and December 2022

keyPoints.point: Students learn that an annual average is the sum of the 12 monthly index values divided by 12
keyPoints.quote: Annual averages are the sum of the 12 monthly data points (i.e. index values), divided by 12

keyPoints.point: Students learn that an over-the-year percent change is not equal to the sum of the over-the-month changes between those periods
keyPoints.quote: is not equal to the sum of the over-the-month changes between those two time periods

keyTerms.gloss: change in an index expressed as a percentage of the earlier value
keyTerms.quote: Movements of an index from one month to another are usually expressed as percent changes rather than as changes in the index value

keyTerms.gloss: value of the index for a single month that is used when you subtract the earlier value and divide by it
keyTerms.quote: you first subtract the earlier index value from the later one, then divide that difference by the earlier index value

keyTerms.gloss: average level for a year found by adding monthly data points and divided by 12
keyTerms.quote: Annual averages are the sum of the 12 monthly data points (i.e. index values), divided by 12

keyTerms.gloss: reference period with index set to 100 used as consistent base for comparison
keyTerms.quote: Always use the same reference base period for all calculations

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Students practice the multi-step procedure in taught order to build accurate calculation habits
componentPlan.focusQuote: you first subtract the earlier index value from the later one, then divide that difference by the earlier index value

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Table work helps students read index values and verify step results against source data
componentPlan.focusQuote: Table 1, 1-month percent change in CPI-U U.S. city average series for all items
